Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=-18x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=-18 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x) & ⇒ & v=\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (-18x)\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =(-18x)\cdot \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\int \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\cdot (-18)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}(-18x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =-6x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /3}+6{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-6x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /3}-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =-6(\frac{\pi }{3}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )-0\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(0))-2(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =-6(\frac{\pi }{3}\cdot 0-0\cdot 0)-2(-1-1) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
